newsitem.title: LEBANON: Monitors say Lebanon rockets hit Israel.
newsitem.headline: Monitors say Lebanon rockets hit Israel.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon said on Tuesday at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel last week but it did not reprimand Lebanon.

The group, comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel said the attack last Friday violated an April 26 ceasefire understanding that bans firing Katyushas at Israel, but it did not specifically hold Lebanon responsible.
The Katyusha was the first fired at northern Israel since the ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon that killed some 200 people, mostly civilians.
The pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God), which fired volleys of Katyushas at Israel before the ceasefire, has denied responsibility for the firing.
Three Palestinian groups in Lebanon made similar denials and the originators of the attack, which caused no damage or casualties, have not been identified.

"By unanimity, the Monitoring Group accepted as factual that at least one Katyusha rocket was fired into Israel from the area of El-Kleila in Lebanon," the monitoring group said after a day-long meeting on Monday to discuss an Israeli complaint about the incident.
"It noted that this act ran counter to the April 26 understanding," it added in a statement.
The group met in the coastal town of Naqoura, headquarters of U.N. peacekeeping troops in south Lebanon.
It said the Lebanese government would do its utmost to ensure compliance with the ceasefire understanding consistent with its commitment to it and its responsibilities under it.

The monitoring group has previously held Israel responsible three times for shelling south Lebanon villages, in violation of a ban in the ceasefire understanding on attacking civilian areas, and has twice deplored the injuries caused by the shelling.
